## Goal

Connect the atomic absorption/emission signal path to an elemental quantity,
recognise spectral overlap, and calculate copper per original dry mass with
correct dilution and method-blank bases. Explain why elemental detection does
not establish original molecular identity or digestion recovery.

## Background

Atomic absorption measures attenuation of suitable source light by free atoms.
Optical emission measures light produced by an excited population. Atomisation
and excitation change the sample; a copper amount does not identify the original
copper-binding molecule or oxidation state. Flame AAS, graphite-furnace AAS and
ICP-OES differ in introduction and atomisation/excitation conditions.

The supplied elemental case calibrates introduced-solution copper in mg/L from
emission counts. A dry sample is digested to a known volume, then diluted again
before measurement. The method blank is a separate digest measured without
that further dilution. Undo the sample dilution **before** subtracting the blank
on a common digest concentration basis. All data and spectra are simulated.

## By hand

**B1.** Write the signal path for AAS and for ICP optical emission. Which uses
an element-specific light source, and which observes light emitted after plasma
excitation? State one kind of chemical information atomisation does not retain.
[Hint](#hint-b1)

**B2.** A 0.2500 g dry sample is made to 50.00 mL digest. Its twofold dilution
measures 0.40189 mg/L copper. The undiluted method blank is 0.001992 mg/L.
Calculate corrected digest concentration, copper amount and mg/kg dry mass.
[Hint](#hint-b2)

**B3.** A second sample uses 0.2000 g dry material made to 25.00 mL. A fivefold
dilution measures 0.0800 mg/L; undiluted method blank is 0.0100 mg/L. Calculate
the result and explain why the blank is not multiplied by five. [Hint](#hint-b3)

**B4.** A dissolved independent check recovers 100%. Does this establish complete
plant digestion? Could a sample-specific neighbouring line still bias the
sample while the simple check passes? [Hint](#hint-b4)

## Explore {#explore}

The spectral model uses Gaussian lines on an offset axis, not authentic copper
identification spectra. The isolated comparison line is idealised to share the
same calibrated sensitivity without interference. Its output is a **diagnostic
apparent result**, not validated reporting permission.

## In R

Run the complete workflow at the project root in a fresh R session. A raw
instrument offset represented by the calibration intercept is different from
contamination measured by the whole-procedure method blank.

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
standards <- read_csv("data/course/atomic-standards.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fit <- lm(emission_counts ~ copper_mg_l, data = standards)
a <- unname(coef(fit)[1]); b <- unname(coef(fit)[2])
qc <- read_csv("data/course/atomic-qc.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(estimated_mg_l = (emission_counts - a) / b,
         recovery_percent = 100 * estimated_mg_l / reference_mg_l,
         qc_pass = recovery_percent >= recovery_lower &
                   recovery_percent <= recovery_upper)
digests <- read_csv("data/course/atomic-digests.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
blank_digest_mg_l <- (digests$emission_counts[digests$sample_id == "method_blank"] - a) / b
results <- digests |>
  mutate(candidate_measured_mg_l = (emission_counts - a) / b,
         in_range = candidate_measured_mg_l >= 0 & candidate_measured_mg_l <= 2,
         corrected_digest_mg_l = candidate_measured_mg_l * further_dilution - blank_digest_mg_l,
         copper_mg_kg = if_else(sample_id != "method_blank" & in_range & all(qc$qc_pass),
           corrected_digest_mg_l * (digest_ml / 1000) / (dry_mass_g / 1000), NA_real_))
ggplot(standards, aes(copper_mg_l, emission_counts)) + geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = a, slope = b) +
  labs(x = "Copper in introduced solution (mg/L)", y = "Emission counts") +
  theme_minimal()
qc
results
write_csv(results, "output/atomic-methods-exercise.csv", na = "NA")
```

**R1.** Interpret the calibration basis and independent-check recoveries.
Why are those checks not plant recovery validation? [Hint](#hint-r1)

**R2.** Report A1 and A2 on the correct original dry-mass basis. Explain the
method blank's missing sample mass and why it has no mg/kg sample result.
[Hint](#hint-r2)

**R3.** List the main uncertainty and recovery evidence missing from these point
estimates. Distinguish elemental copper from original copper species, and explain
why a stable response is not proof of selectivity. [Hint](#hint-r3)

## Hints

::: {#hint-b1 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="B1: follow the photons"}
AAS transmits a source beam through free atoms. ICP-OES observes emitted light
from an excited plasma population. Neither preserves molecular identity.
:::
::: {#hint-b2 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="B2: make the bases agree"}
Multiply sample measured concentration by two, then subtract the undiluted blank.
Use litres for digest volume and kilograms for original mass.
:::
::: {#hint-b3 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="B3: the blank has its own history"}
The blank's concentration already refers to undiluted digest. It did not undergo
the sample's later fivefold dilution.
:::
::: {#hint-b4 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="B4: trace the check material"}
A dissolved reference bypasses the destruction and extraction of native plant
material. It need not contain the sample's interfering element or matrix.
:::
::: {#hint-e1 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="E1: contribution at the selected wavelength"}
An interferer's peak maximum is not the only place it contributes. Its tail can
add signal at the target wavelength.
:::
::: {#hint-e2 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="E2: two different backgrounds"}
The method blank models material introduced during preparation. The sample's
spectral neighbour is a separate contribution absent from that blank.
:::
::: {#hint-e3 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="E3: an ideal alternative is not a free instrument correction"}
Compare to the known model truth, but remember a real alternative line needs
its own interference/background evaluation and appropriate calibration.
:::
::: {#hint-r1 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="R1: count the reference path"}
[`lm`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) relates counts to copper in the introduced
solution. The check does not recreate the original plant digestion.
:::
::: {#hint-r2 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="R2: convert the denominator"}
One gram is $10^{-3}$ kg. The blank is not a plant sample with zero or unknown
true sample mass; it has no meaningful dry-mass denominator.
:::
::: {#hint-r3 .callout-tip collapse="true" title="R3: distinguish a point estimate from validation"}
Consider sampling, native recovery, weighing, volumes, calibration, blank
variation and spectral/matrix effects.
:::

## Solutions

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Full worked solutions"}
**B1.** AAS: element-specific source → free-atom population → wavelength
selection → transmitted-light detector. ICP-OES: sample aerosol → plasma
atomisation/excitation → emission-wavelength separation → detector. Original
molecular identity and oxidation-state distribution are not established by the
resulting total elemental signal.

**B2.** Digest concentration is $0.40189\times2-0.001992=0.801788$ mg/L.
Copper amount is $0.801788\times0.05000=0.0400894$ mg. Dividing by 0.0002500 kg
gives **160.3576 mg/kg dry mass**. The result differs slightly from the later
full-precision R value because the hand inputs were rounded.

**B3.** Corrected digest is $0.0800\times5-0.0100=0.3900$ mg/L. Amount is
0.009750 mg, and dividing by 0.0002000 kg gives **48.75 mg/kg dry mass**.
Multiplying the undiluted blank by five would invent a dilution it never had.

**B4.** No. A dissolved check can recover quantitatively while native plant
copper remains incompletely recovered. A spectral neighbour present only in
the sample can also bias a target signal while a simple check passes.

**E1.** At fixed peak height, moving the interferer away reduces its Gaussian
tail at zero offset. Apparent introduced concentration and apparent dry-mass
result approach the true contribution. Looking only at the selected count
hides why it changed; the neighbouring spectrum gives relevant interference
evidence.

**E2.** Blank subtraction removes the known digest blank on its own basis.
It does not remove the sample-specific overlapping line. Both omitted blank
correction and spectral overlap can bias high, but they require different
chemical evidence and remedies.

**E3.** With ideal isolation and correct blank subtraction, the model always
returns **160.00 mg/kg**: native digest 0.800 mg/L × 0.05000 L / 0.0002500 kg.
Omitting blank subtraction increases the result by blank mg/L × 200. The
alternative line is assumed equal-sensitivity and interference-free here; real
work requires appropriate calibration, background and spectral/matrix checks.

**R1.** The line maps emission response to **mg Cu/L introduced solution** over
0–2 mg/L. Checks recover about **100.37% and 100.77%**, within the supplied
95–105% exercise rule. They do not establish native plant digestion, sample
selectivity or a complete uncertainty budget.

**R2.** Full-precision results are **160.3587** and **300.4236 mg Cu/kg dry
mass**. The method blank has no original plant mass, so its mg/kg field is `NA`.
It supplies a preparation background estimate rather than an elemental result
for a hypothetical zero-mass plant.

**R3.** The point estimates assume quantitative digestion/transfer, appropriate
calibration and selected-signal specificity. A complete evaluation would need
sampling/recovery evidence and relevant uncertainties in mass, volume,
calibration and blank response, including correlations where relevant. Stable
counts show repeatability, not necessarily chemical specificity. Copper amount
does not identify the original molecule or oxidation state.
:::
